limitations: Chord timeouts run on the scheduler's virtual clock: real windows clear chords on the next key or focus change but do not idle-timeout until real wall-clock timers land (the shutdown-integration ticket); deterministic tests drive the virtual clock.

Dead-key and AltGr detection ports process_key line-for-line (ToUnicode with live state, the modifier-cleared comparison) but is verified only through the layout-independent translation paths: injected PostMessage key events cannot fake GetKeyboardState, and SendInput needs a genuinely focused foreground window. Real AltGr/dead-key interaction is a blocked-environment row until a focused-input harness exists; the layout report and all layout-independent paths are verified against the real machine.

The dispatch tree is built during element prepaint (the reference registers listeners at paint and focus at prepaint, both onto the window's node stack); the port's node spans the children within prepaint, which reproduces the same tree shape and ordering.

View-identity dispatch nodes (set_view_id) are recorded by the tree API but no element pushes them yet; the ticket21 accessibility tree wires view nodes. The root view's element nesting (ViewOf adapter) is transparent to the dispatch path.

focusedHandles stub from ticket11 (div.go) replaced by the window focus runtime; window-scoped handle storage remains per-window (the reference keeps one app-global focus map), recorded in focus.go's header.

The keyboard-layout-change callback is per-window (WindowOptions.OnKeyboardLayoutChange) rather than the reference's platform-level singleton; the Go host owns both roles on the same thread, so ordering is identical.
